market_implied_expectations: valuation/05_reverse-dcf.md inverts the module's own DCF (WACC 9.5857%, terminal g 4.0%, 6-yr horizon, FY2025 normalized FCFF base $4,526mm, mid-year convention, all held fixed) and solves (scipy.optimize.brentq, executed not eyeballed) for what the $68.18 price requires: a 14.7% FCFF CAGR over FY2026-2031, equivalent to a 12.8% steady-state EBIT margin on the consensus revenue path -- both below the module's own consensus-anchored DCF base case (18.6% CAGR / 16.0% terminal margin, which independently produces an $82.87 fair value) and only ~65bps above the LTM EBIT margin (12.1%) Uber has already posted. Robustness checks show the FCFF-base assumption is the dominant swing factor (9.2pp spread across a bear/bull Adjusted-EBITDA-derived base), more than the WACC (7.8pp) or terminal-g (3.1pp) sensitivities -- and a mandatory terminal-g sensitivity was triggered because the underlying DCF's terminal value is 77.1% of EV (above the module's own 75% threshold), which independently caps valuation confidence at 60/100. In plain terms: the price requires Uber to hold, not grow, its already-elevated margin -- a conservative bar by the module's own read.
engine_view: valuation/99_valuation-synthesis.md: base-case fair value $74.91/share (peer-relative method, 68% weight, on a 4-name core marketplace set -- Lyft, DoorDash, DiDi, Grab -- at a quality-adjusted 13.25x NTM EV/EBITDA vs today's 11.89x and the raw peer median 14.42x); Bull $104.89 (15.0x); Bear-cyclical (12-month headline) $40.23 (10.0x, toward Lyft's 7.94x); Bear-structural (24-36 month avoid-ruin floor, memo-only, not blended) $31.88. Cross-method single-point dispersion spans $73.39 (peers) to $95.73 (SOTP best-comp), 30%; including each method's stated low/high range the spread widens to $51.15 (SOTP conservative-comp) to $115.44 (own-history, zero-weighted, illustrative-only) -- reconciled by the module as a comparable-selection artefact (which named peer is credited to which segment), not a fundamental disagreement, but still evidence of real noise around the point estimate. Valuation confidence is explicitly capped at 58/100 by the DCF terminal-value-dominance rule. Margin of safety to base case: +9.0% (thin). Downside to the cyclical bear: 41.0% (53.2% to the structural floor) -- a stated 0.20x risk/reward. The synthesis's own verdict: 'Fairly valued... at its edge; genuine borderline case with modestly undervalued one point away.' Separately and non-negotiably, management-governance's RF-CAP-004 (Critical materiality, serial-acquirer pattern culminating in the debt-funded $14.8bn Delivery Hero deal) caps the master rating at Watchlist under CLAUDE.md §24 Filter 4 regardless of how the valuation debate above resolves.
what_everyone_knows: Uber is the largest global ride-hailing/delivery marketplace, has turned durably profitable (operating income -$1,832mm FY2022 to $5,565mm FY2025), is buying back stock, and has signed a large, debt-funded, publicly announced acquisition of Delivery Hero (2026-07-16). Driver-classification regulatory risk and the AV-partnership (not owned-technology) strategy are widely discussed. Two straight quarters of Revenue missing the Street alongside two straight quarters of Adjusted EBITDA beating guidance's high end are both already visible in the reported print history.
what_is_priced_in: A conservative growth/margin case, per the reverse-DCF: 14.7% FCFF CAGR and a 12.8% terminal EBIT margin, both below the sell-side's own consensus base case (18.6%/16.0%) and only marginally above what Uber already delivers (12.1% LTM). The 'no moat proven' finding (3-year average ROIC 6.2% below an ~8.1% WACC estimate) and the serial-acquirer capital-allocation risk are plausibly already contributing to the -17.5% NTM EV/EBITDA discount to the peer set. Separately, sell-side analysts' own mean target price ($102.03, 47 estimates) is well above both the current price and the engine's own $74.91 base fair value -- the sell side, as measured by target prices, is already pricing in more optimism than the engine's peer-relative model grants.
what_market_may_be_missing: The final_thesis identifies three candidate blind spots, none of which constitutes a bullish variant view: (1) the Delivery Hero bridge facility's forward covenant compression (0.9%-25.5% EBITDA-decline breach threshold once drawn, per balance-sheet-survival's stress test) is invisible in every currently reported balance-sheet ratio because the debt has not been drawn; (2) SG&A leverage -- the single largest quantified earnings sensitivity (+/-$780mm) -- has already begun reversing (LTM ratio 20.50% vs the FY2025 low of 19.87%) ahead of a headline miss; (3) the ~10pp Gross-Bookings-to-Revenue growth gap (+22% vs +12.2%) remains unreconciled against any primary filing; management's 'optical, UK reclassification' explanation is stated but unverified. All three are cautionary/risk-flagging, not upside-identifying -- they argue the market's already-cautious bar may still be too generous, not that consensus is underestimating Uber.
evidence_engine_is_different: The reverse-DCF's own math (14.7% implied FCFF growth vs Uber's already-posted 12.1% LTM EBIT margin) is genuine, executed evidence, not opinion -- but it shows the market's implied bar is ACHIEVABLE, which is a statement about downside protection, not a discovered mispricing the market has missed (the same evidence is available to any analyst reading the same Capital IQ consensus, and sell-side target prices at $102.03 mean show the Street is already MORE optimistic than the engine's own $74.91 base case, not less). The three 'market may be missing' items above rest on internal cross-checks of the SAME public data pool (Capital IQ exports, the one available earnings transcript) rather than a differentiated primary-source read -- no primary 10-K/10-Q, no channel check, no alt-data panel, and no expert call exist in data/UBER/ to ground a genuinely proprietary view. The Delivery Hero deal itself has been public knowledge since 2026-07-16; flagging its bridge-facility covenant risk is prudent analysis, not a variant perception the market lacks -- sophisticated holders of the bonds/bridge facility are, if anything, better positioned than this engine to have priced that risk.
base_rate_check: The module's own moat read already applies correct base-rate discipline per CLAUDE.md §9: it tests ROIC against WACC over a 3-year average (6.2% vs ~8.1%), not a single strong year, and notes only 2 of 3 years individually clear the bar -- the correct through-cycle test, matching unit (return on capital), level (consolidated, appropriate since Mobility/Delivery are not separately capitalized), and period (trailing 3 years, not a cherry-picked peak). Uber's own revenue CAGR has been decelerating (18.1% FY23-25 to 12.2% latest quarter) while margin has expanded every quarter for 2+ years -- the base-case assumption of a modest re-rating (11.89x to 13.25x, still below the raw 14.42x peer median) is a moderate, not extreme, extrapolation relative to Uber's own multiple history (though that own-history series is only 17 months/7 quarters and is zero-weighted for being too short to be a reliable base rate itself). No exceptional forecast is being made without exceptional evidence here -- the base case is deliberately conservative relative to the raw peer median -- but the base-rate discipline that IS present argues for caution on the bull case's durability, reinforcing Weak rather than Moderate/Strong variant perception.
notes: Independent re-read (not deferring to the run's own edge_score=40, though the two land in the same weak-edge zone): the base-case valuation gap (+9.9%, $74.91 vs $68.18) sits just inside the module's own +/-10% 'fairly valued' band and is smaller than the noise surrounding it -- cross-method single-point dispersion is 30% ($73.39-$95.73), widening to a >120% spread ($51.15-$115.44) once each method's stated range is included; the DCF backing part of that range is confidence-capped at 60/100 for terminal-value dominance (77.1% of EV); and the margin of safety (9.0%) is roughly a quarter of the downside to the cyclical bear case (41.0%), a 0.20x risk/reward the final_thesis itself calls 'a genuinely poor ratio.' The reverse-DCF finding (price requires only 14.7% FCFF growth / 12.8% margin, both below what Uber already delivers) is real and executed, not eyeballed, but it demonstrates the market's bar is conservative -- it does not by itself demonstrate the engine holds a differentiated view the market lacks, especially since sell-side consensus target prices (mean $102.03, 47 analysts) are already MORE bullish than the engine's own $74.91 base fair value. That gap between sell-side targets and the engine's own valuation is itself worth flagging: either the Street's price targets carry the usual sell-side optimism bias the engine should discount, or the engine's peer-relative method (quality-haircut applied for the unproven moat) is more conservative than the market consensus already is -- either way it undercuts a 'the market is missing something bullish' narrative. The three items the thesis frames as 'what the market may be missing' (DH bridge covenant compression, SG&A reversal, the bookings-revenue gap) are all cautionary and already derived from the same public Capital IQ pool everyone else can read -- no primary filing, channel check, or alt-data source exists in data/UBER/ to ground a genuinely proprietary edge. Combined with the non-bypassable RF-CAP-004 Critical-materiality serial-acquirer cap (CLAUDE.md §24 Filter 4), which caps the headline at Watchlist regardless of how the valuation debate resolves, this is not an exploitable mispricing today. This assessment corroborates the run's own edge_score=40/below-threshold finding and, if anything, is slightly more skeptical of it because the consensus-target-price comparison (not explicitly weighed in the run's own edge discussion) further weakens the 'market is missing upside' framing. There is no proven variant perception yet.
